The '''Halberd-441''', also known as '''Arrogantus-X Skyblade-221 swoop bike''', was a model of [[swoop]] bike manufactured by [[Caelli-Merced]]. Like other swoop models, it was little more than an engine with seats. The Halberd-441 was manned by a single pilot and featured a sidecar for a passenger. It was notably used by [[Tayshin Maxa]] and [[Baroosh Pawk]], members of the [[Cloud-Riders|Cloud-Rider]] gang led by [[Enfys Nest]].<ref name="TOG" />

==History==
In [[10 BBY]],<ref name="Date ref">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' dates the events on [[Vandor]] in ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' to nine years after the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the formation of the Empire to [[19 BBY]]; therefore, the events on Vandor in ''Solo'' must take place in [[10 BBY]].</ref> Pawk and Maxa traveled aboard a Halberd-441 swoop bike with the other Cloud-Riders to the icy [[Planet|world]] of [[Vandor]] in order to attempt to steal a shipment of the [[Fuel|hyperfuel]] [[coaxium]] from the [[Galactic Empire]] with the intention of using it to fund resistance against the Empire and the [[Five Crime Syndicates]]. The gang descended upon the [[20-T Railcrawler conveyex transport]] [[ICC-5537]], which was carrying the coaxium across the [[Iridium Mountains|Iridium]] [[Mountain]]s to [[Crispin Imperial Depository]]; however, they discovered that they were beaten to their target by a [[Beckett's gang|group]] of criminals led by [[Tobias Beckett]] and working for Crimson Dawn.<ref name="Solo">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>

[[File:Halberd441.png|thumb|left|250px|Baroosh Pawk and Tayshin Maxa aboard their Halberd-441]]
The two groups exchanged fire, while Nest dismounted onto the train. Maxa approached the [[Y-45 armored transport hauler]] piloted by [[Rio Durant]] with her swoop bike. She drew her swoop close enough to their adversary's [[starship]] to allow Pawk to leap aboard. After her partner dismounted, Maxa rejoined the other Cloud-Riders in assaulting the conveyed train and helped fire grappling hooks onto the transport car carrying the coaxium. The opposing gang of criminals then lifted the car with the Y-45 armored transport hauler, and it hung between the two groups as they attempted to escape. When the groups drew close to a mountain, the new pilot of the hauler, [[Han Solo]], lost his nerve and released the car, forcing the Cloud-Riders to do the same and leaving the prize to tumble into the mountainside. To escape the ensuing explosion, the Cloud-Riders were then forced to withdraw from the planet empty-handed. Maxa fled Vandor aboard the Halberd-441 without Pawk, who perished in the skirmish.<ref name="Solo" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:M68_Engines.png|thumb|right|250px|The shared engine part of the Halberd-441 and M-68 landspeeder]]
The Halberd-441 [[swoop]] bike first appeared in the [[2018]] film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' and was first identified as the [[Caelli-Merced]] Halberd-441 in the accompanying reference book ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''.<ref name="TOG" /> It was one of several swoop models created for the movie and was referred to by the production team as "The Sidecar" or "The Skiff." The Halberd-441 used the same engine parts as [[Han Solo]]'s [[M-68 landspeeder]], with a few modifications.<ref name="Heist">{{HomeVideoCite|film=Solo|featurette=The Train Heist}}</ref>

The swoop model shares its name with [[Serji-X Arrogantus]], the founder of the original version of the [[Cloud-Riders/Legends|Cloud-Riders]] created by [[Marvel Entertainment|Marvel Comics]] in [[1977]].
